subject: OregonHealth: Special retention request & proof-of-delete workflow
messages:
From: Lydia Grant <lydia.grant@oregonhealth.org>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Eric Tanaka <eric.tanaka@oregonhealth.org>
Date: 2026-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: tenant-specific retention exception + evidence for SOC2/SIG

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. We kicked this to our security and compliance team and have a follow-up ask: several of our integration tenants will need extended log retention for regulatory forensics (state reporting and internal investigations). Specifically: two tenant IDs will require 180-day retention for session/debug traces tied to clinical workflows.

Questions we need answered to proceed with a procurement request:
- Can Redwood support tenant-scoped retention exceptions (longer than default retention) without a full Private deployment?
- If yes, what artifacts do you provide as proof-of-delete or proof-of-preservation post-retention window (e.g., deletion manifests, signed timestamps, hashes)?
- What is the minimum timeline and gating items (legal, runbook, conservancy/controls) for such an exception?

I've attached our SIG/CAIQ matrix with highlights (column B) to show the control mappings where we need evidence.

Attachment: OregonHealth_SIG_questions.xlsx (XLSX)

Appreciate any high-level guidance and who on your side we should loop in for compliance runbooks and engineering scope.

Best,
Lydia Grant
Senior InfoSec Manager
OregonHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Grant <lydia.grant@oregonhealth.org>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-specific retention exception + evidence for SOC2/SIG

Lydia — thanks for the clear ask and the SIG file. Short answer: yes, we can support tenant-specific retention carveouts on hosted accounts in many cases, but there are operational and contractual items to align. Below is a practical breakdown.

Default behavior (hosted):
- Session/request traces and ephemeral debug artifacts: 30 days by default.
- Persistent audit logs and billing/usage: 365 days (accessible via console/export).

What we can offer for a tenant-specific 180-day retention:
1) Per-tenant retention policy override that extends selected trace classes to 180 days (applies only to the specified tenant IDs).
2) Compensating controls we will require: role-restricted access (RBAC), export-to-customer-s3 option, and periodic attestation emails.
3) Proof artifacts: after deletion we can provide a deletion manifest containing: file path inventory, record counts, SHA256 hashes, and a timestamped signature issued by Redwood's HSM-backed signing key. (Engineering may need a short lead time to enable HSM signing in your tenancy.)

Gating and timeline:
- Legal/MAD (mutual action plan): we typically require a signed MAD that defines scope, retention windows, tenant IDs, and retention end triggers.
- Engineering: 2-3 weeks for configuration and audit pipeline changes; 3-4 weeks if HSM-signed manifests are required.
- Compliance runbook and attestation: ~1 week to finalize sample evidence templates.

Estimated next steps and cost signals:
- Provide tenant IDs + desired window (you already said two tenants, 180 days).
- We will produce a carveout runbook and sample evidence.
- One-time integration fee for HSM signing + runbook onboarding may apply depending on scale.

Attachments: redwood-retention-process.pdf (PDF) — high-level retention flows; MAD-template.docx (DOCX) — editable mutual action plan template.

I am looping in Priyom (solutions) and Kimberly (compliance) to handle runbook and evidence specifics. Priyom/Kim — can you confirm the feasibility of producing HSM-signed manifests and an estimated engineering lead time if the customer requires it?

Luca (our CTO) also prefers that we keep an export-to-customer-s3 option as a fall-back for immutable forensic stores.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with your security team to walk through the artifacts.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Grant <lydia.grant@oregonhealth.org>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Eric Tanaka <eric.tanaka@oregonhealth.org>
Date: 2026-05-02T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-specific retention exception + evidence for SOC2/SIG

Thanks Ben — that helps. A couple clarifications from our auditor:
- Scope: tenant IDs OH-TENANT-452 and OH-TENANT-453 only. The 180-day retention is limited to session traces and debug payloads that are directly associated with clinical events; other debug artifacts can remain on the default window.
- Proof-of-delete: auditor specifically asked for signed deletion manifests (SHA256), and either a Redwood-attested timestamp or a signature that can be independently verified. They also want the option to receive a copy to a locked S3 bucket we control (read-only for Redwood).

Are the signed manifests and S3 export options mutually exclusive? Ideally we want both — an HSM-signed manifest stored in our S3 and a Redwood deletion certificate.

If you can, please include:
- A short example of the deletion manifest format (fields and a one-line example).
- Any limits on retention carveouts (e.g., number of tenants, retention classes).

Finally, our procurement team will want to see if the MAD needs to change the SLA (we can escalate if needed).

Appreciate it,
Lydia

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Grant <lydia.grant@oregonhealth.org>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-specific retention exception + evidence for SOC2/SIG

Folks — looping in Compliance (Stephanie) and Solutions (Priyom) to commit to specifics. Short replies inline:

1) Signed manifests + S3 export: not mutually exclusive. We can generate the HSM-signed manifest and optionally deliver a copy to a customer-controlled S3 bucket (read-only role for Redwood). That combination satisfies most auditors.

2) Example manifest (one-line simplified):
- manifest_v1.json: {"tenant_id":"OH-TENANT-452","deleted_at":"2027-11-01T02:15:23Z","records_deleted":12458,"sha256":"3b7f...9a2c","signature":"sig_v1_base64=="}

3) Limits and operational notes:
- Tenant carveouts: we support carveouts up to the account quota (we normally allow up to 10 carved tenants on hosted plans; larger counts require Dedicated or Private).
- Retention classes: we can scope carveouts to specific artifact classes (session traces, debug payloads, KV-cache dumps, etc.).
- Evidence retention: deletion manifests and audit trails are stored in our evidence retention store for 24 months for Redwood audit purposes; customer-delivered S3 copies remain per your controls.

4) Timeline & effort:
- If the customer only needs policy overrides + S3 export: 2 weeks to deliver.
- If HSM-signed manifests are required: 3-4 weeks (engineering change and security review).

5) Contract/SLA: expanding retention for select tenants does not automatically change uptime SLAs, but the MAD should explicitly list retention carveouts and evidence obligations. Our legal ops typically approves a short MAD amendment; if the customer wants Redwood to guarantee retention-as-a-service beyond hosted norms we treat that as an add-on and note potential pricing.

Next steps (to keep momentum):
- Lydia: please confirm tenant IDs you want covered (you already provided them; confirming final).
- Procurement: send a PO or confirm MAD edits.
- Priyom/Engineering: we'll schedule a 30-minute tech call to confirm artifact formats and S3 config.

Attachments: carveout-runbook.md (MD) — draft runbook; compliance-evidence-sample.zip (ZIP) — sample manifests and certs.

Priyom/Stephanie — can you confirm if we need a short security review checklist before enabling HSM signing for this account? If yes, estimate required docs.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Grant <lydia.grant@oregonhealth.org>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Eric Tanaka <eric.tanaka@oregonhealth.org>, AuditSquad Portal <platform@auditsquad.com>
Date: 2026-05-05T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-specific retention exception & proof-of-delete workflow

Ben / team — thanks. We reviewed internally and want to proceed with the following summary:

- Scope: OH-TENANT-452 and OH-TENANT-453; 180 days for session traces and debug payloads tied to clinical event IDs only.
- Evidence: HSM-signed deletion manifests + deliver a copy to our locked S3 (read-only to Redwood); also acceptance of Redwood deletion certificate.
- Timeline: we agree to the estimated 3-4 week window if HSM signing is required.

Procurement will prepare a PO and we will sign the MAD if you produce an editable MAD (the template you attached looks good). Please go ahead and open a tech kickoff and security review. We will add AuditSquad to the evidence delivery channel (they may consume the S3 copy for external audit).

DocuSign link for a quick MAD amendment: https://docusign.example.com/embedded-sign/abc123

Thanks again — please schedule the kickoff.

Lydia Grant
Senior InfoSec Manager
OregonHealth
